vulnerability_analysis: The GoldHunt contract has a rebase function that allows the owner to mint new tokens to the rewardsPool address. The rebase function calculates the current balance of rewardsPool, then mints additional tokens equal to rewardsPoolAmount * (multiple - 1). This means if rewardsPool has X tokens and we call rebase(2), it mints X more tokens to rewardsPool, effectively doubling its balance. The owner controls rewardsPool via setRewardsPool().
attack_strategy: 1. Become the owner (or impersonate the current owner). 2. Set rewardsPool to an address we control. 3. Ensure rewardsPool has some tokens (transfer some from owner or mint). 4. Call rebase() with multiple > 1 to mint new tokens to our controlled rewardsPool. 5. Transfer the newly minted tokens to the attacker address.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the current owner. 2. Call setRewardsPool() to set rewardsPool to attacker address. 3. Transfer some tokens from owner to rewardsPool (attacker) to have a base balance. 4. Call rebase(2) to double the tokens in rewardsPool. 5. Transfer all tokens from rewardsPool to attacker address.

To avoid this, we need to either: 1) Set up the contract properly (router, marketing wallet, etc.), or 2) Use the freeTaxDict to avoid taxes/swaps. Since we're impersonating the owner, we can add our address to freeTaxDict first.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate owner. 2. Set rewardsPool to attacker. 3. Add attacker to freeTaxDict to avoid taxes/swaps. 4. Transfer some tokens from owner to attacker (now tax-free). 5. Call rebase(2) to double attacker's tokens.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Get current owner. 2. Impersonate owner. 3. Call setRewardsPool(attacker). 4. Call setFreeTaxAddress(attacker). 5. Transfer tokens from owner to attacker (now tax-free). 6. Call rebase(2). 7. Verify balance increased.

failure_reflection: The transfer is still triggering swaps even with freeTaxDict. This is because shouldSwap() checks if contract balance > _swapThreshold and swapEnabled is true. We need to disable swapping first.
